title_en: Extradition Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of ensuring the normal progress of extradition, strengthening international cooperation in penalizing crime, protecting the lawful rights and interests of individuals and organizations, and safeguarding national interests and social order.
Article 2 Extradition between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall be carried out in accordance with this Law.

Article 3 The People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall conduct extradition cooperation on the basis of equality and mutual benefit.
Extradition cooperation shall not impair the sovereignty, security and social public interests of the People's Republic of China.

Article 4 Extradition between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall be contacted through diplomatic channels. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China shall be the designated liaison authority for extradition.
If there are special provisions in the extradition treaty regarding the liaison authority, the provisions of the treaty shall be followed.

Article 5 In handling extradition cases, compulsory measures of extradition detention, extradition arrest or extradition residential surveillance may be taken against the person sought for extradition, depending on the circumstances.

Article 47 Where a request is made to a foreign country for granting extradition or transit extradition, the adjudication, procuratorial, public security, state security or prison administration authorities of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government responsible for handling the relevant case shall submit opinions to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security or the Ministry of Justice, respectively, together with relevant documents and materials and their certified translations. After the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security or the Ministry of Justice, together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, examine and approve the request, it shall be submitted to the foreign country through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 48 In an emergency, prior to making a formal request for extradition to a foreign country, a request may be made to the foreign country through diplomatic channels or other channels agreed by the requested country to take compulsory measures against the person concerned in advance.

Article 49 The instruments, documents and materials required for a request for extradition, transit extradition or taking compulsory measures shall be submitted in accordance with the provisions of the extradition treaty. If there is no extradition treaty or there are no provisions in the extradition treaty, the request may be submitted with reference to the provisions of Section 2, Section 4 and Section 7 of Chapter II of this Law. If the requested country has special requirements, the request may be submitted in accordance with the special requirements of the requested country, provided that the basic principles of the laws of the People's Republic of China are not violated.

Article 50 If the requested country attaches conditions to granting extradition, and the conditions do not impair the sovereignty, national interests or public interests of the People's Republic of China, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may, on behalf of the Government of the People's Republic of China, make a commitment to the requested country. A commitment restricting prosecution shall be decided by the Supreme People's Procuratorate; a commitment regarding sentencing shall be decided by the Supreme People's Court.
When investigating criminal liability against the person extradited, the judicial authorities shall be bound by the commitment made.

Article 51 The public security organ shall be responsible for receiving the person extradited by the foreign country and the property relating to the case.
For extradition requests made by other departments, after receiving the person extradited and the property relating to the case, the public security organ shall promptly transfer them to the department that made the extradition request; it may also receive the person extradited and the property relating to the case together with the relevant departments.

Article 52 Where, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the decision on whether to extradite is made by the State Council, the State Council may, when necessary, authorize the relevant departments of the State Council to make the decision.

Article 53 If after making a request, the requesting State withdraws or abandons the extradition request, or if the extradition request is erroneous and causes damage to the person sought for extradition, and the person sought for extradition claims compensation, the claim shall be made against the requesting State.

Article 54 Expenses incurred in handling extradition cases shall be handled in accordance with the extradition treaty or agreement jointly acceded to or concluded by the requesting State and the requested State.
Article 55 This Law shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
